About the Project: As part of long-term investments in Georgia Power’s statewide transmission system, this project includes rebuilding the existing approximately 2.5‑mile Decatur – Scottdale 115 kV transmission line between the Scottdale Substation in DeKalb County and the Decatur Substation on East College Avenue, as well as relocating approximately 0.7 miles of line. This is a rebuild project driven by the age of the existing infrastructure, which was originally constructed in 1965. This project is part of Georgia Power’s ongoing commitment to strengthen and expand the electric grid. By replacing aging infrastructure with more modern materials and design, the project will enhance system reliability, support Georgia’s evolving energy needs, and help ensure safe, resilient electric service for decades to come.

About the Project: Georgia Power is planning the Hills Bridge–Speedway 500 kV Transmission Project in Henry and Clayton counties to support the electric needs of a data center customer that requires new transmission infrastructure, while also strengthening the local electric grid in a rapidly growing area. The project currently includes construction of three transmission lines, one 500 kV line and two 230 kV lines, as well as two new substations, Hills Bridge 500/230 kV Substation and Speedway 230 kV Substation. Together, these improvements will add capacity, enhance reliability for homes and businesses, and position the region to support continued growth and evolving energy needs.

O’Hara–Scherer 500 kV Transmission Line (Hills Bridge Loop): Approximately .25 mile of new 500 kV transmission line in Clayton County connecting the new substation to existing transmission facilities. Hills Bridge–Speedway #1 230 kV Transmission Line: Approximately 1.5 miles of new 230 kV transmission line in Henry and Clayton counties. About the Project: The Conyers – Klondike 230 kV project consists of a new 8.5-mile transmission line that will run between the Conyers Substation in Rockdale County and the Klondike Substation in Dekalb County. In some locations, the Conyers–Klondike 230 kV transmission line will follow the existing Conyers - Klondike 230 kV transmission corridor. In other areas, a new corridor will be created where required by the project design. This project is part of our ongoing commitment to strengthen and expand the electric grid. This critical infrastructure is designed to enhance system reliability, support Georgia’s evolving energy needs, and ensure safe, resilient service for decades to come.
